objectClass.notes: Hard-surface object. Every corner carries a ~45 degree chamfer; this facet language is the identity, not smooth fillets. Body tapers slightly inward toward the top. Single three-quarter view: rear face, left face, and underside are inferred by symmetry and carry reduced confidence.

reasoning: Six distinct meso parts: body shell, top bezel, slot cavity, base plinth, lever, dial.
Two repetition systems: nine dial tick marks and six internal element tabs in the cavity.
Action readiness is high because this becomes a launching trap: the lever and carriage must animate and the toast is ejected.
Occlusion risk is moderate: only one view, so rear and left faces are inferred from symmetry.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Rear face detail is not visible; assumed plain shell matching the front.
Underside and foot geometry are not visible; four corner feet inferred from the plinth silhouette.
Cavity depth is not measurable from this view; set to a plausible fraction of body height.

detailInventory.scanMethod: component-zone scan of the three-quarter reference at 3x and 4x magnification, cross-checked against per-material crops
detailInventory.note: Every detail below resolves to a component.localFeatures id or a material.localOverrides id; none is prose only.

details.description: Every vertical and horizontal corner of the shell carries a wide flat 45 degree chamfer, giving a faceted octagonal plan rather than a rounded box.
details.geometryRecipe: Extruded Shape with a chamfered plan outline; never a rounded box.

details.description: The shell narrows by 0.03 units per side between the plinth seam and the top of the vertical wall, about 3.8 percent on the width.
details.geometryRecipe: profileStops scale the shape-plane coordinates along the extrusion axis.

details.description: A 0.14 unit tall chamfer band insets the plan a further 0.11 units before the flat top deck begins.
details.geometryRecipe: Final profileStop turns the top of the prism into a frustum band.

details.description: The coral bezel stands 0.055 units above the cream deck and frames the opening as a chamfered rounded-rectangle ring.
details.geometryRecipe: Extruded octagonal ring with a hole, seated 0.02 units into the deck.

details.description: The bezel crown chamfers inward by 0.03 units instead of rounding over.
details.geometryRecipe: Final profileStop on the bezel extrusion.

details.description: Six small dark tabs project from the slot walls, three per slot, reading as heating element brackets.
details.geometryRecipe: InstancedMesh of six boxes in two rows of three.

details.description: The divider stops 0.08 units below the rim so its lit crown reads as a pale strip along the opening.
details.geometryRecipe: Box partition whose top ends below the deck plane.

details.description: Nine short coral tick marks ring the rotary dial; the plinth hides the lowest three, so the reference reads as an arc.
details.geometryRecipe: InstancedMesh of nine boxes on a radial placement about the dial axis.

details.description: A raised rib runs from the knob centre toward its rim and marks the current setting.
details.geometryRecipe: Box bar parented to the knob so it turns with it.

details.description: The yellow lever rides in a channel whose floor sits 0.036 units below the surrounding collar crown, visible above and below the knob.
details.geometryRecipe: Proud collar ring with a chamfered-rect opening and a dark floor plate behind it.

details.description: Every edge of the yellow knob carries a flat chamfer about 0.06 units wide.
details.geometryRecipe: Chamfered-rect extrude profile plus an end-chamfer profileStop.

details.description: The coral plinth is 0.05 units wider than the shell on every side and carries its own chamfer, reading as a separate slab.
details.geometryRecipe: Separate chamfered extrude, wider footprint, 0.02 unit seam overlap into the shell.

details.description: Both the top and the bottom edge of the plinth bevel inward by 0.05 units.
Four small pads at the plinth corners lift it 0.06 units off the counter.
details.geometryRecipe: Four box pads inset from the plinth corner facets. Two are visible; two are inferred.

details.description: A hard contact shadow runs along the joint where the cream shell enters the coral plinth.
details.geometryRecipe: Material local override raising roughness and AO in the lowest 0.05 units of the wall.

details.description: The slot pocket darkens sharply with depth; the floor is the darkest value in the frame.
details.geometryRecipe: Material local override with a depth-driven AO boost on the pocket walls.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
